dedupe_keys.name: madis meteorological assimilation data ingest system noaa including mesonet and dot road weather stations

description: MADIS is a meteorological observation database and delivery system run operationally at NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Prediction. It ingests data from NOAA and non-NOAA providers, decodes them into a common format with uniform units and time stamps, runs quality checks and stores the results with flags. Partners include international agencies, federal, state and local agencies such as state departments of transportation, universities, volunteer networks and private firms such as airlines and railroads; surface data include thousands of mesonet stations, some restricted. Data can be requested from July 2001, and all MADIS data are being added to the NOAA archive. The restrictions page sets distribution tiers, some for government, research and education only. Coverage: mainly the Americas, with global feeds. Format and access: several access methods after application. Licence and cost: free, with tiered restrictions. Caveats: road weather station coverage depends on DOT participation. It supports hazard exposure and emergency response studies of weather on roads and aviation. It relates to the Danish road weather feeds in the catalogue.
